ap_precalculus-f01.title: Exponential function, its inverse and a composition

stimulus.description: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=4\cdot 2^x+5$ for $x\ge 0$, and the function $g$ is defined by $g(x)=3x-2$. A graphing calculator is required for these questions.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find the value of $f(2)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of f at the given input

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The function $f$ is invertible. Find the value of $f^{-1}(40)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up the equation f(x) = target, or isolates the exponential and takes a logarithm
alt_solutions: log base b of (target minus k over a)

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of the inverse

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Find all values of $x\ge 0$ for which $g(f(x))=90$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Composition g(f(x)) written with f substituted into g and set equal to the target
Solution value

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Does $f$ have a horizontal asymptote as $x$ increases without bound? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: No. The base of the exponential term is greater than 1, so the exponential term grows without bound as $x$ increases and so does $f(x)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that there is no horizontal asymptote because the exponential term grows without bound for a base greater than 1
common_errors: claims y = k is a horizontal asymptote on the right

ap_precalculus-f02.title: Test score modeled by a logarithmic function

stimulus.description: A student's score $L(t)$ on a vocabulary test, in points, after $t$ hours of study is modeled by $L(t)=30+25\ln(t+1)$ for $t\ge 0$. A graphing calculator is required for these questions.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find $L(9)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of the function at the given input

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $L$ over the interval $1\le t\le 7$. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of your answer in the context of the problem.

rubric_rows.criterion: Average rate of change value
Interpretation with units: average increase in score per hour over the interval

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: For what value of $t$ does the model give a score of $96$ points?

rubric_rows.criterion: Equation setting the model equal to the target score

parts.prompt: The average rate of change of $L$ over $1\le t\le 3$ is greater than the average rate of change over $5\le t\le 7$. What does this say about how the score changes as the number of hours of study increases?
parts.model_answer: The average rate over $1\le t\le 3$ is about 8.664 and over $5\le t\le 7$ about 3.596; the score keeps increasing but at a decreasing rate.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the score increases at a decreasing rate, supported by the two average rates of change
